frontier.hypothesis: The function closes on the NEW candidate chassis as soon as one insn class other than a giv initial value can be emitted between loop.c's movables and NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG - i.e. as soon as the two p-copies land after `li 5 / li 20` while the walker stays a SOURCE pseudo (which is what gives it the 11 refs the allocation needs).
frontier.mechanism: move_movables inserts movables immediately before loop_start, after every pre-loop source statement; strength_reduce's emit_iv_add_mult then emits giv initial values after them. Those are the only two loop.c insertion points measured so far, and the giv class is forbidden by this session's allocation arithmetic (9 refs can only tie, and ties go to the counter). The next probe is forensic on loop.c itself, not on spellings already swept.
frontier.next_probe: Instrument tools/gcc-2.7.2/loop.c with a BB2-style env-gated hook at every emit_insn_before(loop_start)-class call site (move_movables, strength_reduce/emit_iv_add_mult, loop_iterations/biv initialisation, final-value replacement) and print what each emits for func_8003504C on both chassis. Then ask which of those classes can carry a pointer that is ALSO referenced after the loop - e.g. whether a biv whose final value is used after the loop gets its initialisation emitted at loop_start rather than as a pre-loop statement. Any class that does is the win.

frontier.hypothesis: The h1 chassis (score 9, whole residual = the i/p-walker swap) still closes if the counter's allocno priority can be pushed below 9310 by a post-loop reuse that survives copy propagation and costs no instruction.
frontier.mechanism: pri = floor_log2(refs)*refs/live_length with cc1's own numbers; the counter is 11/33 = 10000 and the giv is 9/29 = 9310. Only reuses with two joining definitions survive propagation (adjacent def/use pairs are folded), and the reuse must reach far enough out: (refs 12, len >= 39), (13, >= 42), (14, >= 46), (15, >= 49). v_a1 (sel) reached 14/43 = 9767, three insns of live range short.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate post-loop reuse sites in the val==2 and val==5 arms that produce two joining definitions (conditional value selections and the loop-2 setup), generate one variant per site, and read pri(pseudo 73) straight off tmp/grind/func_8003504C/s7/alloc.sh - no sandbox run needed to reject a site. Only variants with pri < 9310 AND build_insns == 141 need scoring; on h1 such a variant is a full match, since the swap is its only residual.

frontier.hypothesis: A decomp-permuter campaign seeded on the NEW candidate chassis is worth one run: it is a strictly better base than session 4's ws3 (four differing positions instead of seven, and target's register assignment already in place).
frontier.mechanism: Session 4 showed random search finds levers of exactly this shape when the chassis is close (the src-reuse find came out of ws2 at 132 s); session 4's ws3 ran 20373 iterations with no find, but that was on the seven-position chassis whose residual included the base/ptr pre-loop statements this chassis no longer has.
frontier.next_probe: Rebuild a workspace with tmp/grind/func_8003504C/s4/mkws.sh + mkbase.sh from the new candidate.c, record the permuter base score (session 4's chassis was 120), run a fresh-seed campaign with tools/permuter_campaign.py, and wait for it in-session with `permuter_campaign.py wait`; harvest and --stop before ending the turn. Any find that moves the two `li`s ahead of the p-copies is the answer.
